# Header layouts

Generated by `cargo xtask layouts --write` (VER-072); `cargo xtask layouts` and `cargo xtask ci` check that this file is current. Each layout is derived from the encoders and decoders of the codec crates, not from a second table: the probe encodes a header, changes one field at a time, and records which bits change. A field the encoder never changes (a version number, a reserved spare) takes the bits for which the decoder rejects a change, naming the field. The probe fails if two fields share a bit or a bit belongs to no field. The field names, codes, and clauses are those of the rustdoc of the items ([RS-015](../06-verification.md)) and of the field catalogue ([03 §9.1](../03-api-model.md#91-field-codes)).

Bits are numbered as the Blue Books number them: bit 0 is the most significant bit of the first octet. A bit range of `first–last` runs over consecutive bits; a field in several ranges is split in the header. The clauses cite the Blue Books by document number; this file quotes none of their text or figures.

Not covered: the AOS edition of Issue 4 and earlier (bits 42–43 are a reserved spare), the M_PDU and B_PDU headers, the FHEC and OCF fields beyond what the headers above show, the extension octets of a P-field and the P-field of an agency-defined code (their bits are defined by the agency or by the code), and the ASCII time codes, to which `aldis-time` gives no P-field.
